stem: A 35-year-old man presents with fatigue, pallor, pica, and spoon-shaped nails. Laboratory tests reveal microcytic hypochromic anemia. Which of the following best explains the underlying pathophysiology of his condition?
stemHtml: A 35-year-old man presents with fatigue, pallor, pica, and spoon-shaped nails. Laboratory tests reveal microcytic hypochromic anemia. Which of the following best explains the underlying pathophysiology of his condition? (Question Id: 501018)
keywords: Spoon-shaped nails (koilonychia) – Classic physical sign of chronic iron deficiency.
Pica – Craving for non-food items; strongly suggests iron deficiency anemia.
Microcytic hypochromic anemia – Lab hallmark indicating impaired hemoglobin synthesis.
keywordsHtml:
1. Spoon-shaped nails (koilonychia) – Classic physical sign of chronic iron deficiency.
  2. Pica – Craving for non-food items; strongly suggests iron deficiency anemia.
  3. Microcytic hypochromic anemia – Lab hallmark indicating impaired hemoglobin synthesis.

C.title: Impaired hemoglobin synthesis
C.body:
The most common cause of impaired hemoglobin synthesis is iron deficiency. Iron is required for the production of the heme component of hemoglobin. A lack of iron results in less hemoglobin being incorporated into the RBCs, causing them to be hypochromic (pale). The bone marrow also tries to compensate by making smaller cells, resulting in microcytic (small) anemia. The patient's symptoms (fatigue, pallor) and signs (pica, spoon-shaped nails or koilonychia) are highly suggestive of chronic IDA.
Lab findings: low serum ferritin, low serum iron, high TIBC.
Key concept: The anemia is due to inability to incorporate iron into hemoglobin, not RBC destruction or deficiency of B12/folate.
C.bodyHtml:
• The most common cause of impaired hemoglobin synthesis is iron deficiency. Iron is required for the production of the heme component of hemoglobin. A lack of iron results in less hemoglobin being incorporated into the RBCs, causing them to be hypochromic (pale). The bone marrow also tries to compensate by making smaller cells, resulting in microcytic (small) anemia. The patient's symptoms (fatigue, pallor) and signs (pica, spoon-shaped nails or koilonychia) are highly suggestive of chronic IDA.
  • Lab findings: low serum ferritin, low serum iron, high TIBC.
  • Key concept: The anemia is due to inability to incorporate iron into hemoglobin, not RBC destruction or deficiency of B12/folate.

A.title: Hemolysis
A.body:
Hemolysis refers to premature destruction of red blood cells.
Usually presents with jaundice, reticulocytosis, elevated LDH, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia.
Does not typically cause spoon-shaped nails or pica.
A.bodyHtml:
• Hemolysis refers to premature destruction of red blood cells.
  • Usually presents with jaundice, reticulocytosis, elevated LDH, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia.
  • Does not typically cause spoon-shaped nails or pica.

B.title: Autoimmune destruction
B.body:
Seen in autoimmune hemolytic anemia (e.g., warm or cold antibody-mediated).
Causes hemolysis with positive Coombs test.
Microcytic anemia is not a feature.
B.bodyHtml:
• Seen in autoimmune hemolytic anemia (e.g., warm or cold antibody-mediated).
  • Causes hemolysis with positive Coombs test.
  • Microcytic anemia is not a feature.

D.title: Folate deficiency
D.body:
Causes macrocytic anemia (megaloblastic).
May present with glossitis, fatigue, but nails are not spoon-shaped.
Microcytosis and pica are uncommon.
D.bodyHtml:
• Causes macrocytic anemia (megaloblastic).
  • May present with glossitis, fatigue, but nails are not spoon-shaped.
  • Microcytosis and pica are uncommon.

E.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency
E.body:
Also causes macrocytic, megaloblastic anemia.
May have neurologic symptoms (paresthesia, balance issues).
Does not cause spoon-shaped nails or pica.
E.bodyHtml:
• Also causes macrocytic, megaloblastic anemia.
  • May have neurologic symptoms (paresthesia, balance issues).
  • Does not cause spoon-shaped nails or pica.

keyConcept: Iron deficiency anemia is a microcytic hypochromic anemia caused by impaired hemoglobin synthesis. Clinical clues include fatigue, pallor, pica, and koilonychia. Lab confirmation is with low serum ferritin and iron, high TIBC.

diagram.name: (Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia)
diagram.caption: This diagram illustrates the pathophysiology of iron deficiency leading to impaired hemoglobin synthesis, resulting in microcytic hypochromic red blood cells. It highlights key clinical features (fatigue, pica, koilonychia), characteristic laboratory findings (low hemoglobin, low ferritin, high TIBC), and the mainstay of treatment with iron supplementation.
